Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testNan()` asserts that the expression "$nan > $nan" should evaluate to Boolean.FALSE. The current bug report also states that comparing NaN with NaN returns true, but it should return false, which contradicts IEEE floating point comparison semantics where NaN compared to anything (including itself) is false.

From the code snippets retrieved, the evaluation of the "greater than" operation is done in `CoreOperationGreaterThan.evaluateCompare(int)` which returns `compare > 0`. The `evaluateCompare` method receives an integer representing the comparison of two operands, where positive means left operand is greater than right operand.

The root cause lies in how the comparison integer is computed for operands that are NaN. The comparison integer should not indicate greater than zero when comparing NaN with NaN. However, this logic is presumably handled in a broader comparison method that returns the integer input to `evaluateCompare`.

This broader comparison logic is not yet obtained, but it is likely done in the code before `evaluateCompare` is called in some method responsible for producing the comparison integer. The bug is that when both operands are NaN, the comparison method inaccurately returns a positive integer rather than indicating unordered (or equivalently a special case for NaN to return 0 or a negative number).

Hence, the incorrect comparison result stems from the comparison logic of the two operands when both are NaN. Fixing needs to add a NaN check in the operand comparison method before returning the comparison integer to ensure NaN compared to anything is never treated as "greater than".

Recent bug reports do not mention NaN or numeric comparisons, so they are irrelevant in this context.

Next, I should locate the method responsible for producing the integer comparison result that is passed into `evaluateCompare`. It might be a generic compare method. After finding it, checking for NaN handling or absence thereof will finalize the diagnosis.

Thus, the likely faulty area is the operand comparison logic that produces the comparison integer (which is input to `evaluateCompare`), not the simple `evaluateCompare` methods themselves, which only interpret the comparison integer.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
